_readme: Every number the model uses that is NOT pulled live lives here. Edit this file, not the code. Dollar figures are in $ millions. The reasoning behind each input is in the README under 'Assumptions and why'.

fundamentals_fy2026._source: Costco FY2026 earnings release (Sept 24, 2026). DCF base year.

wacc_inputs._note: risk-free rate and beta are replaced by live values when online; the fallbacks are used offline.

dcf_base_case._note: Three-stage FCFF model. Years 1-5: growth fades 8% to 6% as the fee increase laps. Years 6-10: growth fades from 6% to the 3% long-term rate as new openings shrink relative to a bigger base. After year 10: Gordon-growth terminal value at 3%. Margins rise to 4.1% by year 5 and hold. Reinvestment = change in revenue / sales_to_capital.

scenarios._note: Monte Carlo draws each input independently from a triangular distribution (bear, base, bull). Why these ranges: the whole 10-year growth path shifts by up to 4 points either way, so year-1 growth runs from 4% to 12% (FY2026 was 10.1%). Margin -0.5%/+1.0% runs from about 3.6% (below FY2026's 3.85%) to about 5.1%, which covers the 'margins reach 5%' bull case. WACC +/-1.5% is wider than the sensitivity table. Terminal growth 2% to 4% brackets long-run nominal GDP.

reverse_dcf._note: Growth rate used for the 'how many years of high growth' version of the reverse DCF. 10% is roughly FY2026's pace.

bull_case._note: Every bull lever stacked at once, to test whether the price is justified even if things go right: 10 years of growth fading from 9% to 8%, margins rising to 4.8% (ads, e-commerce, Kirkland, fee hikes), then the same kind of 5-year fade down to the 3% long-term rate the base case uses, and a discount rate 1 point below the live WACC for Costco's safety and low beta.

rating_rule._note: Rating from target vs price: BUY above +10%, SELL below -10%, otherwise HOLD.
